trial_title: Quality Improvement Intervention to Promote Early Mobilization in Trauma ICU
brief_summary:
Background: Despite the fact that many lines of evidence point to the safety and feasibility of early mobilization in medical or surgical ICUs, there remains limited evidence regarding the efficacy or outcome of mobilizing patients in trauma ICU. Given the lack of published literature or routine protocol for mobilizing this population in our institution, the investigators developed a formal protocol and quality improvement project.

eligibility_table.criterion: patients >20 years of age admitted to the trauma ICU (more than 3 days)
who were alive more than 7 days after ICU admission
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has a history of ICU admission, but it is unclear if they survived more than 7 days after admission.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient been alive for more than 7 days following ICU admission?

eligibility_table.criterion: patients < 20 years old who required trauma ICU admission for less than three days

eligibility_table.justification: The patient's current status post-ICU admission is not provided, making it uncertain if they died after ICU admission.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Did the patient die within 30 days of ICU admission?

eligibility_table.justification: No lab values in patient profile
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of less than 6?

eligibility_table.justification: No lab values in patient profile
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient experienced a raised intracranial pressure measurement exceeding 20 mmHg at any point during their ICU stay?

eligibility_table.justification: There is no information provided regarding cardiopulmonary arrest in the patient's history.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Did the patient experience a cardiopulmonary arrest during their ICU stay?

eligibility_table.justification: There is no information provided regarding acute myocardial infarction in the patient's history.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient been mobilized within 48 hours of ICU admission following their acute myocardial infarction?

eligibility_table.justification: There is no information provided regarding rapidly developing neuromuscular disease in the patient's history.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient experienced any signs of rapidly developing neuromuscular disease, such as significant muscle weakness or respiratory failure, within the last 30 days?

eligibility_table.justification: There is no information provided regarding pregnancy in the patient's history.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Is the patient currently pregnant or has she been pregnant within the last 12 months?

eligibility_table.criterion: with ruptured or leaking aortic aneurysm
eligibility_table.justification: There is no information provided regarding ruptured or leaking aortic aneurysm in the patient's history.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient experienced a ruptured or leaking aortic aneurysm within the last 30 days?

eligibility_table.criterion: ICU admission for palliative care or medical orders specifying alternate activities
eligibility_table.justification: There is no information provided regarding the reason for ICU admission, making it unclear if it was for palliative care.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient been admitted to the ICU with medical orders specifying palliative care or alternate activities within the first 24 hours of admission?
